summary.prose: This Story lets a tool declare the shape of its input and result, and makes the executor check both before the tool runs and before anything sees its result. It adds a typed call helper so workflow code gets a result whose type comes from the declared shape, a conversion library that turns text-only CLI output into that shape with a cheap model and checks the key values against the raw text, and one set of failure kinds. A tool that code never calls keeps its text output and is not checked.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Alternative a1: the executor in src/daemon/tools/executor.ts becomes the one pipeline for all external operations, and git, gh and Jira (acli) are registry tool families with an optional declared output schema and an approval class (none, common or destructive). Workflow and daemon code call tools through a typed helper that takes the tool definition; about 32 production files that spawn git or gh, or call a wrapper that does, move onto it in one change.

ownedContracts.name: Tool output schema and typed call
ownedContracts.purpose: Lets a tool declare its result shape, has the executor check it when declared, and gives callers a result typed from the tool definition they pass.

ownedContracts.name: Text conversion with cross-check
ownedContracts.purpose: Turns text-only CLI output into the declared shape using the cheap model, cross-checks the key values against the raw text, and escalates once to a higher-tier model; conversions run serially.

ownedContracts.name: CLI failure kinds
ownedContracts.purpose: One set of failure kinds returned by every git, gh and acli tool so callers tell a missing CLI, a missing sign-in, a time-out and a rejection apart.
ownedContracts.interfaceSketch:
type ToolFailureKind = 'missing-tool' | 'missing-signin' | 'unreachable' | 'timed-out' | 'rejected' | 'conversion-failed' | 'schema-mismatch' | 'denied'
interface ToolFailure { kind: ToolFailureKind; message: string; denial?: ApprovalDenial }

boundary.internal: The optional output-schema field and the check at step 4 of the pipeline, the typed call helper that takes a tool definition, the serial conversion queue, the key-value cross-check and the one-time escalation, and the shared failure kinds. It includes the choice of schema language and the way an input-to-tool mismatch is reported. It does not declare or read the approval class.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The hook stage inside executeTool: the registry of hooks keyed by tool id, registration order, the rule that a hook runs only after a successful, checked call, and the way a hook failure is carried on the result. It places its stage at step 5 of the pipeline order in the architecture shape and does not own the schema check or the approval step.

The approval step at step 2 of the pipeline: the single approval field on a tool definition, the global approval setting for the common class and its default, the IPC request and answer methods, the timeout value, the daemon-side holder of the pending requests, the terminal-client, editor and chat implementations of the answer, and removal of the 'auto-approving' fallback in executor.ts. It maps every existing requiresApproval flag, in every family, to the common class, and lists the tools that change. It does not choose which individual git, gh or Jira operations are destructive; each family Story marks its own.

The list of git operation families, their input and output schemas, which git operations are in the destructive class (for example force push, hard reset, clean, deleting a branch or tag), and the parsing of git porcelain output. Operations that need approval but cannot destroy work stay in the common class. Existing git ids keep their meaning.

The list of gh operation families, their schemas (read from gh --json where it exists, converted from text otherwise, for example gh pr diff and gh run view --log), which of the 27 gh operations that need approval are in the destructive class, and the 120 second time limit and its message. Existing gh ids keep their meaning.

The Jira tool families over acli (work item view, search, create, edit, transition, assign, comment, link, project list and view), their schemas, the --yes flag on every mutating command, the bounded forms of search and project list that acli requires, the 'acli jira auth status' sign-in check, and which operations are in the destructive class. An operation acli does not offer is left out and named as unsupported.

The repository check that fails on a direct git, gh or acli spawn outside src/daemon/tools, built first; the inventory it produces (about 32 production files known today, with the indexer, the design corpus reader, the analyze ignore filter, the understanding identity lookup and the daemon self-update included and no allowlist); the rewrite of every listed site and of the tests that import the old wrappers onto the typed helper; and the removal of runGit, commitAndPushArtifacts and the github.ts wrappers. It keeps the artifacts, commits and tracker records the same as before.

nonFunctional.performance: gh commands time out after 120 seconds (decided with the user; the daemon is expected to become multi-threaded so a slow gh will not block it). The approval wait has its own timeout, set in s3's LLD. Conversion is serial, so a text-only tool that needs the cheap model costs one model call per attempt plus at most one escalated call; structured-output tools make no model call.
nonFunctional.security: No argument, setting, environment variable or caller identity can skip the approval for a destructive call; with no client attached the call is denied. Common calls follow one global setting. Approval requests travel only over the daemon's Unix socket. No credentials are read or stored: gh, git and acli use the user's own CLI sessions. A tool that declares an output schema and returns a result that does not match it fails and its result is not passed on. Today the executor runs every tool flagged requiresApproval as approved (11 git tools, 5 more by predicate, 27 gh operations and other families), so nothing asks; this Epic makes destructive calls ask every time and puts the rest under the global setting.
nonFunctional.observability: The executor logs each stage per call with the tool id, the caller, the approval class and decision and its reason, the schema check result, and each hook outcome. Hook failures, denials and conversion escalations are returned to the caller as part of the result, not only logged.
nonFunctional.durability: Pending approval requests are held in memory by the daemon and are lost on restart; a request left open at restart is treated as denied. Hooks are registered in code at start-up, not stored. The global approval setting is stored in the daemon's config. The cutover leaves artifacts, commits and tracker records unchanged.

api.name: callTool
api.signature: export type TypedTool = Tool & { readonly inputSchema: TSchema; readonly outputSchema: TSchema }; export function callTool<T extends TypedTool>(tool: T, input: Static<T['inputSchema']>, deps: ToolDeps): Promise<TypedToolResult<Static<T['outputSchema']>>>

parameters.name: tool
parameters.purpose: The tool definition object the caller imports; its type carries both schemas, so the input and the result are typed from it. A tool whose inputSchema or outputSchema is not a typebox schema does not satisfy TypedTool and is a compile error.

parameters.name: input
parameters.purpose: The tool's input, typed from its inputSchema.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: The tool dependencies; text-only tools read deps.conversion, deps.repoPath and deps.signal from it.

returns.meaning: On success, success true and data typed as the output schema's static type. On any failure, success false, no data, and error holding a ToolFailure with a kind.

errors.condition: No tool is registered under tool.id, or the input does not fit the tool's inputSchema (the message names the failing fields and the tool is not run).
The tool succeeded but its data does not match its outputSchema, or it succeeded without data.
missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, timed-out, rejected or conversion-failed, as the tool reports them; denied comes from the approval step of s3.

preconditions: The tool is registered under tool.id (the same definition object is registered at start-up).
tool.inputSchema and tool.outputSchema are typebox schemas, which the type TypedTool enforces at compile time.
postconditions: callTool never throws for a tool failure; every failure is returned as a ToolFailure.
When success is true, the input and data have passed validation against the schemas, so the cast-free types are true.
callTool adds no model call; a conversion happens only inside a tool that calls convertText.

api.name: executeTool
api.signature: export function executeTool(toolId: string, input: ToolInput, deps: ToolDeps): Promise<ToolResult>

parameters.name: toolId
parameters.purpose: Unchanged: the registered id or alias.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: Unchanged signature; ToolDeps gains the optional conversion field.

returns.meaning: The tool's result. For a tool that declares an outputSchema, this Story adds two checks: the input is validated against inputSchema before the tool runs, and data is validated against outputSchema after it runs (step 4 of the pipeline). A tool without an outputSchema is run and returned exactly as before.

errors.type: ToolResult with success false and failure.kind 'rejected'
errors.condition: The tool declares an outputSchema and the input does not fit its inputSchema; the message names the failing fields and the tool is not run.

errors.type: ToolResult with success false and failure.kind 'schema-mismatch'
errors.condition: The tool declares an outputSchema and data is missing or does not match it; the message names the ajv errors, data is dropped, output is replaced by the message, and failure.original keeps the tool's own output, truncated.

preconditions: Steps 1 to 3 of the pipeline order (resolve, approval, run) belong to the executor and s3; this Story owns the input check that comes with step 1 for schematized tools and the output check at step 4.
postconditions: A tool with no outputSchema returns exactly what it returns today, so every existing builtin and the agent loop at src/agent/read-only-tool-loop.ts:78 behave unchanged.
A failed or denied result is returned untouched and is not validated.
Nothing the hook stage of s1 runs sees an unchecked result.

api.name: convertText
api.signature: export function convertText<S extends TSchema>(req: ConversionRequest<S>, deps: ToolDeps): Promise<ConversionResult<Static<S>>>

parameters.name: req
parameters.purpose: { toolId, rawText, schema: S, keyValues: (value: Static<S>) => string[] }. keyValues is required, so a caller cannot ask for a conversion without naming the values to cross-check.

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: convertText reads deps.conversion (the provider resolver), deps.repoPath and deps.signal; the first is the new optional field, the others exist today.

returns.meaning: { ok: true, value, tier } when a value fits the schema and every key value appears in the raw text; otherwise { ok: false, failure } with a ConversionFailure kind and detail, and the raw text left with the caller.

errors.condition: No attempt produced a value that fits the schema.
A value fits the schema but a key value is not found in the raw text after normalising (whitespace collapsed, case folded, surrounding quotes dropped).

The cheap tier and then the escalated tier both used their attempts without an accepted value, a provider call failed, no deps.conversion is configured ('no conversion provider configured'), the input is too large (the InputTooLargeError case), or the caller cancelled ('cancelled').

preconditions: rawText is non-empty and was produced by a CLI that gives no structured output.
keyValues returns only non-empty strings that are expected to occur verbatim in rawText, such as identifiers, numbers, paths and status words.
postconditions: Calls run one after another through a module-level queue, so no two conversions reach a provider at once, whatever the number of concurrent tool calls (k3).
At most two attempts on the cheap tier and, only if those fail, two on the escalated tier; the attempt count is a constant in the module, not a setting.

A per-attempt deadline surfaces as an ordinary 'timed out' error inside the provider call, so withStructuredRetry retries it; only a caller cancellation surfaces as AbortError and ends the conversion as 'cancelled'.
convertText never throws for a conversion failure.

dataModelChanges.details: Adds an optional outputSchema holding a typebox TSchema. A tool with the field puts its result in ToolResult.data and its text for agents in output, and has its input and data checked by the executor. The HLD sketch said JsonSchema with a phantom output type; typebox derives the type from the schema, so the two cannot disagree. inputSchema keeps its current type on Tool; the type TypedTool requires it to be a typebox schema, which only callers of callTool need. No existing builtin is changed.
Adds an optional failure of type ToolFailure so a failed result carries its kind. success, error and output stay as they are, so the agent loop reads the same fields it reads today.

{ kind: ToolFailureKind; message: string; original?: string; denial?: ToolDenialReason }. ToolFailureKind is the union in sc5: missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, timed-out, rejected, conversion-failed, schema-mismatch, denied. ToolDenialReason is 'declined' | 'timed-out' | 'no-client', declared here so that this Story does not depend on s3; s3 reuses it. original is the tool's raw output, truncated, kept for diagnosis. TypedToolResult<O> is { success: boolean; data?: O; error?: ToolFailure }.

Adds one optional field, conversion, holding { resolveProvider(role: 'tools.convert' | 'tools.convert.escalate'): LLMProvider }. A small helper in the conversion module builds it from an AnalyzeConfig, the repoPath and RoleRouter.resolveProviderForRole, which is synchronous. convertText reads it together with the existing repoPath and signal. A ToolDeps built without it makes a text-only tool fail with 'no conversion provider configured'. Four production places build a ToolDeps today: src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1132, src/agent/providers/ollama.ts:686, src/workflow/code-review/grounding.ts:370 and src/workflow/runners/build/changed-files.ts:110. This Story changes none of them, since the field is optional and none of them runs a text-only tool yet. s7 fills the field in the two workflow-side builders (grounding.ts and changed-files.ts) when it gives them text-only tools.

Adds two roles to the closed registry in the role taxonomy: tools.convert (peripheral, default tier cheap) for the first conversion attempts, and tools.convert.escalate (peripheral, default tier mid) for the single escalation. Both resolve through the RoleRouter and can be reassigned by the user's roleTiers like any role, so the escalation tier is a setting, and mid is only the default. The coreFloor does not apply to peripheral roles.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: { id: 'tools.convert', criticality: 'peripheral', defaultTier: 'cheap' }; { id: 'tools.convert.escalate', criticality: 'peripheral', defaultTier: 'mid' }

dataModelChanges.details: The tracker port's type stays at its four kinds (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected); the port, its stored results and its tests are not changed. Where a tracker adapter calls a tool (s7), it maps a ToolFailureKind onto the port as: missing-tool to missing-tool, missing-signin to missing-signin, unreachable to unreachable, timed-out to unreachable (as src/workflow/tracker/github.ts maps a timeout today, keeping the message 'timed out after N s'), and rejected, conversion-failed, schema-mismatch and denied to rejected, with the tool's message as the reason. This settles review finding 5.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Implements the output-schema field, the executor's input and output checks for schematized tools, and callTool. Refines the HLD sketch: outputSchema is a typebox TSchema, callTool takes a definition typed TypedTool and returns Static of the schemas, and the input is typed from inputSchema, in place of JsonSchema plus a phantom type and an untyped input; consumers s4 to s7 take the definition object, as the HLD already says.

Implements convertText as the sketch states: cheap tier first, deterministic cross-check of the key values, one escalation, one serial queue. Refinements: keyValues is required, the schema is a typebox TSchema, and the function takes the ToolDeps (repoPath, signal and the new conversion field) that the sketch left out and that the RoleRouter call needs.

Implements the failure kinds as the sketch states and adds the mapping onto the tracker port's four kinds. Adds ToolResult.failure, ToolFailure.original and a ToolDenialReason union that ToolFailure.denial uses in place of the ApprovalDenial type owned by s3; proposed to the HLD as a sharedContract.fieldAdd amendment.

errorCases.scenario: The input given to a schematized tool does not fit its inputSchema.
errorCases.detection: Before running a tool that declares an outputSchema, executeTool calls validateAgainstSchema(inputSchema, input) and it returns ok false with the ajv error list.
errorCases.response: Do not run the tool. Return success false with failure kind 'rejected' and a message naming the failing fields; log the tool id.
errorCases.userImpact: A wrong argument from a workflow stage is reported by name and nothing is run, instead of reaching the CLI.

errorCases.scenario: A tool with an outputSchema returns success true but no data.
errorCases.detection: After the run step, executeTool sees the tool has an outputSchema, result.success is true and result.data is undefined.
errorCases.response: Return success false with failure kind 'schema-mismatch' and the message "tool <id> returned no data for its declared output schema"; drop data; keep the tool's own output in failure.original, truncated.
errorCases.userImpact: The caller gets a named failure, not an untyped success; an agent that called the tool sees the message in output. This is a bug in the tool and is found by its test.

errorCases.scenario: A tool's data does not fit its outputSchema.
errorCases.detection: validateAgainstSchema(outputSchema, data) returns ok false with its list of ajv error messages.
errorCases.response: Return success false with failure kind 'schema-mismatch'; the message names the failing paths from the ajv errors; data is dropped; failure.original keeps the tool's output, truncated at a fixed limit (a constant in the module); the failure is logged with the tool id.
errorCases.userImpact: The unmatched result is never passed on (ac2). A workflow stage that needed it fails with a message that says which field is wrong.

errorCases.detection: The existing try/catch in executeTool around tool.execute.
errorCases.response: Unchanged: return success false with the message in output and error, and now also failure kind 'rejected' with the same message. No schema check runs on a failed result.
errorCases.userImpact: Same text as today for agents; code callers get a typed kind.

errorCases.scenario: callTool is given a tool whose id is not registered.
errorCases.detection: executeTool's getTool lookup returns undefined (the existing 'Unknown tool' path).
errorCases.response: Return success false with failure kind 'rejected' and the existing message "No tool registered for '<id>'".
errorCases.userImpact: A wiring mistake at start-up shows as a named failure on first use, not a crash.

errorCases.scenario: A tool declares a schema that ajv cannot compile.
errorCases.detection: validateAgainstSchema throws or reports a compile error the first time the inputSchema or outputSchema is used.
errorCases.response: Treat as a defect in the tool: return success false with failure kind 'rejected' and the message "tool <id> declares an invalid input or output schema", log at error level with the compile message, and do not cache a result for that schema.
errorCases.userImpact: Every call to that tool fails the same way until it is fixed; its test fails first.

errorCases.scenario: A text-only tool calls convertText on a ToolDeps that has no conversion field, for example one built by a workflow-side builder that s7 has not yet updated.
errorCases.detection: convertText finds deps.conversion undefined before it takes a queue slot.
errorCases.response: Return conversion failure 'retries-exhausted' with detail 'no conversion provider configured'; no model call is made; the tool returns failure kind 'conversion-failed'.
errorCases.userImpact: A mis-wired ToolDeps shows as a named failure on the first text-only call, not as a silent fall back to unconverted text.

errorCases.scenario: The cheap tier returns a value that does not fit the schema.
errorCases.detection: validateAgainstSchema returns ok false on the model's output.
errorCases.response: Retry within withStructuredRetry with the ajv errors appended to the prompt, up to two attempts on the tier; if both fail, escalate once to the tools.convert.escalate role for up to two attempts.
errorCases.userImpact: None visible when a later attempt succeeds; the result records tier 'escalated'.

errorCases.scenario: A converted value fits the schema but a key value is not in the raw text.
errorCases.detection: After validation, each string from keyValues is searched in the normalised raw text (whitespace collapsed, case folded, surrounding quotes dropped); one is missing.
errorCases.response: Count the attempt as failed with kind 'value-not-in-text' and retry with the missing values named; after the escalated attempts also fail, return conversion failure 'retries-exhausted' with the last detail; the tool returns failure kind 'conversion-failed' with the raw text in failure.original.
errorCases.userImpact: A made-up identifier or count never reaches a caller (ac6); the caller gets conversion-failed and the original text to read.

errorCases.scenario: No provider can be built for the conversion role, or a provider call fails.
errorCases.detection: RoleRouter.resolveProviderForRole throws, or the provider call rejects, on every attempt.
errorCases.response: Return conversion failure 'retries-exhausted' with detail naming the role and the cause; do not fall back to the unconverted text or to a direct REST call (k1); the tool returns failure kind 'conversion-failed'.
errorCases.userImpact: A text-only tool fails when no local or CLI model is available; tools with structured output are unaffected.

errorCases.detection: A per-attempt deadline (a constant in the module) expires while the queue slot is held.
errorCases.response: Abort the provider call, but raise an ordinary Error with the message 'timed out' from inside the call closure, not an AbortError, so withStructuredRetry treats it as a failed attempt and retries; release the queue slot at the end of every attempt.
errorCases.userImpact: One slow conversion delays the queue by at most the deadline per attempt and cannot block it for good, and a timeout does not end the retry budget.

errorCases.scenario: The caller cancels while a conversion is queued or running.
errorCases.detection: deps.signal is aborted before the queue slot is taken (checked when the slot is granted) or during a provider call (an AbortError raised from the caller's signal, not from the deadline).
errorCases.response: A queued conversion is dropped without calling a provider; a running one is aborted and the AbortError is allowed to end withStructuredRetry; both return conversion failure 'retries-exhausted' with detail 'cancelled'.
errorCases.userImpact: A cancelled workflow stage stops without spending model calls.

errorCases.scenario: The raw text is longer than the model accepts.
errorCases.detection: The provider raises an error named InputTooLargeError, which withStructuredRetry rethrows without resending.
errorCases.response: Return conversion failure 'retries-exhausted' with detail 'input too large'; do not truncate or retry; the tool decides whether to split the text or fail.
errorCases.userImpact: A very long log fails with a clear reason and can be split by the tool's author.

edgeCases.input: A tool with an outputSchema returns success false.
edgeCases.expected: The result passes through unchanged and is not validated; its failure kind and message reach the caller.

edgeCases.input: A tool with no outputSchema is called through executeTool with any input.
edgeCases.expected: The input is not validated and the result is not checked, exactly as today; callTool does not compile for that tool.

edgeCases.input: The tool is called through an alias such as a legacy name.
edgeCases.expected: executeTool resolves the alias, runs and checks the canonical tool; callTool uses the definition's own id.

edgeCases.input: keyValues returns an empty array because the output has nothing checkable, for example 'nothing to commit'.
edgeCases.expected: The value is accepted on schema alone and the log line says no key value was checked; ac6 applies only when a value can be checked.

edgeCases.input: A key value '12' and raw text 'issue 123 created'.
edgeCases.expected: The match is on token boundaries for alphanumeric values, so '12' is not found in '123' and the attempt fails.

edgeCases.input: A key value 'Fix-Login' and raw text 'fix-login' on a line with extra spaces.
edgeCases.expected: Whitespace and case are normalised, so the value is found.

edgeCases.input: Two tool calls ask for a conversion at the same moment.
edgeCases.expected: They run one after another through the module queue in arrival order; neither reaches a provider while the other is in flight.

edgeCases.input: A conversion succeeds on the escalated tier after two cheap failures.
edgeCases.expected: The result is ok with tier 'escalated', and a log line records the escalation and the role that served it.

edgeCases.input: The schema allows additional properties and the model adds an extra field.
edgeCases.expected: validateAgainstSchema does not remove it (removeAdditional is off); tool schemas are written with additionalProperties false, so the extra field fails the check.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A tool with no outputSchema returns exactly what it returns today, its input is not validated, and the agent loop keeps reading output, success and error.
A throw inside tool.execute is caught by executeTool and returned as a failed result, never propagated to the caller.
The existing ToolResult fields (output, format, success, error, data) keep their meaning; failure is additive and optional, and the existing ToolDeps fields keep theirs.
getTool honours aliases and registerTool keeps its overwrite-with-warning behaviour; this Story adds no registration rule.
The four production places that build a ToolDeps keep compiling and behaving as they do, because the conversion field is optional.
validateAgainstSchema does not mutate the payload (removeAdditional off) and caches compiled validators per schema object, so the executor and convertText must pass the same schema object.

withStructuredRetry rethrows AbortError and InputTooLargeError at once and retries any other thrown error, so the conversion must raise a deadline as an ordinary error and let only a real cancellation surface as AbortError.
Reasoning models are built only through the RoleRouter, CliProvider or Ollama, never a direct REST call, and never run in parallel.
The tracker port's PortFailureKind stays the four kinds and the existing unit-issue test that iterates them keeps passing.
Test files stay node:test files under __tests__ run by tsx, which does not type-check; type-level assertions therefore live in a file the build compiles.

testStrategy.testFramework: node:test run with tsx (npx tsx --test), flat test() calls with node:assert/strict, files named *.test.ts under __tests__ next to the code, each with a header comment naming the Story and a 'Run: npx tsx --test <path>' line; live tests gated on INSRC_LIVE_TESTS=1 and skipped cleanly when unset. tsx does not type-check and tsconfig.json excludes **/__tests__/**, so the type-level assertions for ac5 are written as // @ts-expect-error lines in src/daemon/tools/call-tool.type-test.ts, a file outside __tests__ that npm run build (tsc) compiles; it exports nothing and is never imported.

testLevels.purpose: Prove the executor's input and output checks in isolation: a registered fake tool with and without an outputSchema, given valid and invalid input, returning valid data, invalid data, no data and a failure.
subjects: executeTool: valid input and valid data on a schematized tool pass through unchanged
executeTool: input that does not fit the inputSchema returns rejected naming the fields, and the tool is not run
executeTool: data that does not fit returns schema-mismatch, names the ajv paths, drops data, keeps failure.original truncated
executeTool: success without data on a schematized tool returns schema-mismatch
executeTool: a failed result is not validated and passes through
executeTool: a tool with no outputSchema is run and returned exactly as today, with its input unchecked
executeTool: a thrown error still returns a failed result, now with failure kind rejected
executeTool: an invalid inputSchema or outputSchema returns rejected and is logged
failure kinds: the mapping of each ToolFailureKind onto PortFailureKind, one test per kind
fixturesNeeded: A fake Tool factory that returns a chosen ToolResult and records whether it ran
Small typebox schemas (an object with strings and numbers, one with additionalProperties false)
A test registry reset between tests

testLevels.purpose: Prove convertText with fake providers injected through deps.conversion: tiers, retries, escalation, the cross-check, the serial queue, the deadline and cancellation.
subjects: convertText: a first-attempt valid value on the cheap tier returns ok with tier cheap and no escalation
convertText: an invalid first attempt is retried with the ajv errors appended
convertText: two failed cheap attempts escalate once, and two failed escalated attempts return retries-exhausted
convertText: a value that fits the schema but has a key value missing from the raw text fails with value-not-in-text and retries
convertText: key-value matching normalises whitespace and case and drops surrounding quotes
convertText: an alphanumeric key value matches on token boundaries, so '12' is not found in '123'
convertText: an empty keyValues result is accepted on schema alone
convertText: two concurrent calls reach the fake provider one after another, in arrival order
convertText: a ToolDeps with no conversion field returns 'no conversion provider configured' without a model call
convertText: a provider that rejects on every attempt returns retries-exhausted naming the role, with no fallback

migration.stateBefore: executeTool in src/daemon/tools/executor.ts looks a tool up, runs it inside a try/catch and returns its ToolResult (output string, format, success, error, data typed unknown). Tool in src/daemon/tools/types.ts has no output schema, and the executor does not validate input or output although the Tool.inputSchema comment says it validates input. ToolResult has no failure kind and ToolDeps has no conversion field; four production places build a ToolDeps (src/analyze/context/driver.ts:1132, src/agent/providers/ollama.ts:686, src/workflow/code-review/grounding.ts:370, src/workflow/runners/build/changed-files.ts:110). No conversion library exists, and the role taxonomy in src/config/role-taxonomy.ts has no tool-conversion role. The only production caller of executeTool is src/agent/read-only-tool-loop.ts:78, which reads the text output. The tracker port keeps four failure kinds in src/workflow/tracker/port.ts:23. The build excludes **/__tests__/** from type-checking.
migration.stateAfter: Tool has an optional typebox outputSchema, ToolResult has an optional failure and ToolDeps has an optional conversion field. For a tool that declares an outputSchema, executeTool validates the input before the tool runs and the data after, and returns a typed failure on a mismatch; a tool without a schema behaves exactly as before. callTool returns data typed from the definition's schemas and does not compile for a tool without them, and its type-level tests live in a file the build compiles. convertText converts text-only CLI output through the cheap tier then one escalation, cross-checks the key values against the raw text, runs through one serial queue and retries a timeout while ending on a cancellation. Two new peripheral roles, tools.convert and tools.convert.escalate, exist in the role taxonomy. The tracker port's four failure kinds are unchanged, and a stated mapping takes the new kinds onto them. No existing builtin has an output schema, and none of the four ToolDeps builders sets a conversion value; the git, gh and Jira family Stories add schemas, and s7 fills the conversion field in the two workflow-side builders.

migrationSteps.action: Add the optional outputSchema field to Tool, the optional failure field to ToolResult and the optional conversion field to ToolDeps, with the ToolFailure, ToolFailureKind and ToolDenialReason types. Nothing reads them yet, and none of the four ToolDeps builders changes.

Add the two conversion roles to the role taxonomy as peripheral roles with default tiers cheap and mid. Add a taxonomy test that the closed registry lists them and that the coreFloor does not clamp them.

Add the conversion module: the serial queue, the key-value normalisation and token-boundary match, the cheap attempts, the single escalation, the per-attempt deadline raised as an ordinary error, the cancellation handling and the helper that builds the conversion field from a config and the RoleRouter. Add its unit tests with fake providers. No tool calls it yet.

Add the input check and the output check to executeTool, applied only to a tool that declares an outputSchema, and attach failure kind rejected to the existing thrown-error and unknown-tool results. Add the executor unit tests, and run the existing agent-loop and tool tests unchanged.
Add callTool and the TypedTool type, with the type-level test file that the build compiles and the runtime test beside it. No production code calls it until s4 to s7.

Record the mapping of the new failure kinds onto the tracker port's four kinds in the contract notes for s7, and keep the port type and its tests unchanged. Record there that s7 fills the conversion field in the two workflow-side ToolDeps builders.

Apply the approved HLD amendment that adds ToolResult.failure, ToolFailure.original and ToolDenialReason to the sc5 sketch, so the consuming Stories read the final shape and s3 reuses the denial union.

migration.backwardCompat: Every addition is optional: Tool.outputSchema, ToolResult.failure, ToolFailure.original and ToolDeps.conversion. A tool without an outputSchema is run and returned exactly as before, with its input unchecked, so the roughly 110 existing builtins and the agent loop at src/agent/read-only-tool-loop.ts:78 see no change. The only visible difference is on error results: the existing thrown-error and unknown-tool results now also carry failure kind 'rejected'; output, success and error keep their text. The tracker port, its results and its tests are unchanged. The two new taxonomy roles are additive and the router resolves them like any role. The four existing builders of ToolDeps need no change.

alternativesConsidered.name: Optional typebox schemas on Tool, a conversion library that tools call, inputs supplied through one optional ToolDeps field
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Add optional typebox output and input schemas to Tool; the executor validates input and output only for tools that declare an output schema; callTool is typed from the definition; text-only tools call convertText, which gets its providers through one optional ToolDeps field.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Tool in src/daemon/tools/types.ts gains one optional field, outputSchema, holding a typebox schema (TSchema). A tool that declares one puts its structured result in ToolResult.data and its human text in output. For such a tool, and only such a tool, the executor first validates the input against its inputSchema and refuses to run the tool on a mismatch (failure kind 'rejected', the failing field names in the message), and after the run validates data against the outputSchema with the existing validateAgainstSchema helper, turning a mismatch into a failed ToolResult of kind schema-mismatch. A tool with no outputSchema is run and returned exactly as today, so the roughly 110 builtins with loose inputSchemas are untouched. callTool takes a definition typed as TypedTool, a Tool whose inputSchema and outputSchema are both typebox schemas, so an unschematized tool is a compile error at the call site, the input is typed as Static of the inputSchema and the result as Static of the outputSchema (ac5). The failure kinds (sc5) are one union plus a ToolFailure that rides on ToolResult.failure, and a three-value denial union is declared here so that s2 does not depend on s3.

A tool whose CLI gives only text calls convertText(req, deps) while it builds its result (ac4). ToolDeps gains one optional field, conversion, holding a resolveProvider(role) function; a small helper builds it from an AnalyzeConfig, the repoPath and RoleRouter.resolveProviderForRole, which is synchronous. convertText reads deps.conversion, deps.repoPath and deps.signal, runs behind a module-level serial queue (k3), tries the tools.convert role for up to two attempts and the tools.convert.escalate role for up to two more, validates every attempt with the same ajv helper, and checks each key value against the normalised raw text. A per-attempt deadline is turned into an ordinary 'timed out' error inside the provider call so withStructuredRetry retries it; only a caller cancellation is allowed to surface as AbortError and ends the conversion as 'cancelled'. A tool with structured CLI output (gh --json, git porcelain, acli --json) parses it directly and never touches the model (ac3). The type-level tests for ac5 live in a file that tsc compiles, since the build excludes the __tests__ folders. This Story fills no conversion value in any of the four production ToolDeps builders; s7 fills it in the two workflow-side ones.
pros: Smallest change that meets every criterion: two optional fields on Tool and ToolResult, one optional field on ToolDeps, one executor step and two small modules; the roughly 110 existing builtins compile and behave unchanged.

Reuses what exists: validateAgainstSchema and withStructuredRetry for the check and the retry, typebox for derived types, and RoleRouter and the role taxonomy for model choice, so there is no second validator or provider path.
Input validation is limited to tools that declare an output schema, so the executor takes on the HLD's 'input mismatch' duty without risking the builtins whose inputSchema is loose or wrong.

The compile-time guard is plain TypeScript, and the conversion is a function a tool calls while it builds its result, which matches ac4 and lets the tool pre-process the text and name its own key values.
cons: Nothing forces a schematized tool to put its result in data on success: a tool that forgets fails the check at run time with schema-mismatch, not at compile time.
Type inference works only if callers import the definition object; a tool looked up by string id through getTool is typed as plain Tool.
Every text-only tool author must remember to call convertText with key values; a tool that parses text on its own compiles and runs without the cross-check, and only review catches it.

ToolDeps grows by one optional field that the two workflow-side builders (grounding.ts:370 and changed-files.ts:110) must fill when s7 gives them text-only tools, or those tools fail with 'no conversion provider configured'.

alternativesConsidered.name: defineTypedTool factory that makes the schemas and the typed result required by construction
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A defineTypedTool factory takes typebox input and output schemas and a run function that returns the typed value, and builds the Tool, so a schematized tool cannot omit data or its schemas.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
A factory, defineTypedTool({ id, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, run, render }), is added next to Tool. run(input, deps) returns Promise<Static<Output> | ToolFailure>; render(value) produces the text that agents read. The factory returns a Tool whose execute calls run, sets ToolResult.data to the value and ToolResult.output to render(value), and attaches a brand so that callTool accepts only tools made this way. The executor still validates the input and the data, because both come from outside the type system, but the compile-time shape of the tool is guaranteed. Failure kinds are the return type, so a tool cannot throw a bare string for a known failure.

Conversion is offered as a factory option: a tool can declare textOnly: { keyValues } and receive raw CLI text, and the factory calls convertText on its behalf, so no author has to call it or remember the cross-check. Existing builtins stay plain Tool objects; only the git, gh and Jira families, and any tool that code calls, use the factory.
pros: The two mistakes a1 leaves possible, an absent data field and a skipped cross-check, become impossible by construction for factory-made tools.
Authors of the roughly 60 git, gh and Jira tools write a function that returns a typed value, which is simpler than building a ToolResult by hand.
The brand makes the compile-time guard on callTool exact.
cons: Adds a second way to define a tool beside the plain Tool literal, so the codebase has two idioms for as long as the old builtins exist.
Larger surface to design and test (factory generics, brand, render contract, textOnly option) for a Story that has to ship before s4 to s6 can start.
The render function duplicates text the agent path used to build by hand; a tool whose text and data disagree is a new kind of bug.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on sc2: it adds a factory and a brand that consumers must use, which the contract does not state, and it is the larger change for a Story that gates s4 to s6.

alternativesConsidered.name: Plain JSON Schema plus a hand-written output type (the HLD sketch)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep outputSchema as a plain JSON Schema object and carry the TypeScript type as a separate phantom parameter on the tool definition.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Follow the HLD sketch literally: OutputSchemaField<O> has outputSchema?: JsonSchema and a phantom readonly outputType?: O, and callTool infers O from the tool object. Each tool author writes the schema as JSON Schema and, separately, the TypeScript type O, and assigns them to the same definition. The executor validates data with the same ajv helper. Nothing derives one from the other, so the schema and the type are two statements of the same shape. Conversion and failure kinds are the same as in a1.
pros: No dependency on typebox's builder for tool authors; plain JSON Schema is also what the model-provider layer already accepts for completeStructured.
Matches the HLD sketch word for word, so no amendment question arises.
cons: Two statements of one shape that can drift apart: the check passes on the schema while callers trust the hand-written type, which is the failure k2 forbids.
A phantom property with no runtime value is easy to misuse and invisible in review.
Repeats work that typebox's Static already does, with more code in every tool.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on ac5 and k2: the type a caller receives is hand-written and can disagree with the schema the check enforces.

alternativesConsidered.name: Conversion as an executor stage for tools that declare text-only output
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A tool that gets only text declares textOnly and returns raw text; the executor converts and validates it before the tool's result reaches anyone.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Tool gains an optional outputSchema as in a1 and a second optional declaration, textOnly: { keyValues }. A tool with textOnly returns its raw CLI text in ToolResult.output and no data; after the run the executor sees the declaration, calls convertText with the tool's schema, validates, and either sets data to the converted value or fails the call. Tools with structured output set data themselves and skip conversion. The model dependency moves into the executor, which resolves the two providers through the RoleRouter and owns the process-wide serial queue. callTool is typed as in a1.
pros: Tool authors write no model code: a text-only tool is a CLI call that returns text, plus a schema and its key values.
The serial rule (k3) and the escalation live in one place, the executor, with one test target.
cons: The executor, which should stay a small pipeline, takes a model dependency and a provider-resolution step it does not have today; ToolDeps carries only an Ollama provider.

The tool no longer 'builds its result' (ac4): the result is built after the tool returns, so a tool that must pre-process the text, for example to strip ANSI codes or cut a long log, has no hook for it.
Every executeTool call pays for a check on whether conversion is needed, and the stage widens the blast radius the HLD already lists as its first risk.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Partial on ac4 (the conversion happens after the tool returns, not while it builds its result) and sc3 (the executor, not the tool, calls the conversion, which changes how s4 to s6 consume it).

openQuestions: The sc2 and sc3 refinements (a typebox TSchema in place of JsonSchema plus a phantom type, a typed input, a ToolDeps parameter on convertText) differ from the HLD sketches. Only the sc5 additions (ToolResult.failure, ToolFailure.original, ToolDenialReason) are proposed as an HLD amendment, because one proposal is allowed per run; the sc2 and sc3 refinements need their own amendment or a back-flow (audit item sbdry3, partial).

DEF S002 FR001 ('a tool without a declared result shape cannot be registered') and FR004 ('every tool declares the shape of its result') are narrowed by the recorded decision in docs/plans/tool-registry.md that only tools code calls need a schema, enforced at the callTool type. The amendment tool handles HLD amendments only and cannot amend DEF text, so this LLD keeps registration unchanged and asks the reviewer or the user to accept that decision record as the amendment.
The carrier for caller identity (review round 3 finding 4) is not decided here: this Story adds only the conversion field to ToolDeps. It belongs to s1 (the hook context) and s3 (the approval mode).
